claims.text: HFrEF, hydralazine instead of an ACE-I/ARB: 25 mg PO QID, ↑ every 3–5 d to a 300 mg/day target (many can't tolerate > 200 mg/day: hypotension).
claims.quote: When used instead of ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy, hydralazine is started at 25 mg orally 4 times a day and increased every 3 to 5 days to a target total dose of 300 mg/day; however, many patients cannot tolerate > 200 mg/day because of hypotension.

claims.text: Added to an ACE-I/ARB: 37.5 mg TID, max 75 mg TID.
claims.quote: When added to ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy, hydralazine plus nitrate therapy is started at 37.5 mg and isosorbide dinitrate at 20 mg orally 3 times a day, with the maximum dose 75 mg and 40 mg 3 times a day.

claims.text: Nitroprusside: higher mortality than clevidipine, nitroglycerin or nicardipine, so not used when alternatives exist;
claims.quote: Data show increased mortality with nitroprusside compared to clevidipine, nitroglycerin, and nicardipine, and thus nitroprusside should not be used when other alternatives are available.

claims.text: mostly limited to hypertensive acute decompensated HF;
claims.quote: Its use is mostly limited to patients with acute decompensated heart failure who are hypertensive.

claims.text: also hypertensive encephalopathy and, with a beta-blocker, aortic dissection.
claims.quote: It is also used for hypertensive encephalopathy and, with beta-blockers, for aortic dissection.

claims.text: Nitroprusside: usually 0.5–10 mcg/kg/min IV; never more than 10 min at the maximum rate,
claims.quote: The usual dose rate is 0.5 to 10 mcg/kg/min, but infusion at the maximum dose rate should never last more than 10 minutes.

claims.text: and stop if BP isn't controlled by then.
claims.quote: If blood pressure has not been adequately controlled after 10 minutes of infusion at the maximum rate, administration of sodium nitroprusside should be terminated immediately.

claims.text: Only where BP can be monitored continuously.
claims.quote: Sodium nitroprusside should be used only when available equipment and personnel allow blood pressure to be continuously monitored.

claims.text: > 2 mcg/kg/min can accumulate cyanide (agitation, seizures, cardiac instability, anion-gap metabolic acidosis).
claims.quote: However, administration of > 2 mcg/kg/minute can lead to cyanide accumulation with toxicity to the central nervous system and heart; manifestations include agitation, seizures, cardiac instability, and an anion gap metabolic acidosis.

claims.text: Prolonged use (> 1 wk; 3–6 d with renal insufficiency) accumulates thiocyanate (lethargy, tremor, abdominal pain, vomiting):
claims.quote: Prolonged administration of nitroprusside (> 1 week or, in patients with renal insufficiency, 3 to 6 days) leads to accumulation of thiocyanate, which can result in lethargy, tremor, abdominal pain, and vomiting.

claims.text: check levels daily after 3 d and stop if > 12 mg/dL.
claims.quote: Thiocyanate levels should be monitored daily after 3 consecutive days of therapy, and the medication should be stopped if the serum thiocyanate level is > 12 mg/dL (> 2 mmol/L).

claims.text: Hydralazine: CBC and ANA titer before and periodically during prolonged therapy,
claims.quote: Complete blood counts and antinuclear antibody titer determinations are indicated before and periodically during prolonged therapy with hydrALAZINE even though the patient is asymptomatic.

claims.text: and if arthralgia, fever, chest pain or malaise develop.
claims.quote: These studies are also indicated if the patient develops arthralgia, fever, chest pain, continued malaise, or other unexplained signs or symptoms.

claims.text: A lupus-like picture means stopping it unless the benefit clearly requires continuing.
claims.quote: In such patients hydrALAZINE should be discontinued unless the benefit-to-risk determination requires continued antihypertensive therapy with this drug.
